title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: FAYE'S RINK
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Faye Lindgren, fifty-four, a shift boss at a paper mill in Green Bay, Wisconsin.
For twelve winters she looked out her kitchen window at the empty lot next door, and complained.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE EMPTY LOT
segments.quote: Regret for the things we did can be tempered by time; it is regret for the things we did not do that is inconsolable.
segments.author: Sydney J. Harris
lines: As a girl, Faye skated every night on her dad's backyard rink.
Then she found an old newspaper clipping of his, a line from the columnist Sydney J. Harris:
Regret for the things we did can be tempered by time; it is regret for the things we did not do that is inconsolable.
That night, she dragged her garden hose to the lot.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE MUD
segments.quote: Life consists not in holding good cards but in playing those you do hold well.
segments.author: Josh Billings
lines: The water soaked into the dirt. She made a very large mud puddle.
Her neighbor Gus laughed and quoted the old humorist Josh Billings:
Life consists not in holding good cards but in playing those you do hold well.
Faye looked at her cards. A hose. A cold January. Gus's big blue tarp.
She laid the tarp down and tried again.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: FIVE A.M.
segments.quote: I am only one, but still I am one. I cannot do everything, but still I can do something.
segments.author: Edward Everett Hale
lines: Good ice takes thin coats, every night, at twelve below. Nobody wanted to help.
On the mill's break room wall hung a line from Edward Everett Hale:
I am only one, but still I am one. I cannot do everything, but still I can do something.
So every morning at five, before her shift, she sprayed one thin coat. Alone. In two snowsuits.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE BUMPS
segments.quote: Change the way you look at things, and the things you look at change.
segments.author: Wayne Dyer
lines: The ice froze. Lumpy. Like a frozen waffle.
Faye wanted to cry. Then she remembered a line from the author Wayne Dyer:
Change the way you look at things, and the things you look at change.
So she stopped calling it a rink. She painted a sign: The Bumpy Bowl. Broomball only. Falling encouraged.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE FANCY RINK
segments.quote: It is better to fail in originality than to succeed in imitation.
segments.author: Herman Melville
lines: People came. Then Gus said, let's make it like the fancy city rink.
Faye's sister, a librarian, quoted Herman Melville, who wrote Moby-Dick:
It is better to fail in originality than to succeed in imitation.
So the Bumpy Bowl stayed weird. Cocoa in a slow cooker. An old couch on the ice for the grandmas.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE LAST NIGHT
segments.quote: We do not remember days, we remember moments.
segments.author: Cesare Pavese
lines: In March, the thaw came. One last night, the whole block skated under the porch lights.
Gus, who now owns three snowsuits, read a line from the Italian writer Cesare Pavese:
We do not remember days, we remember moments.
Faye rolled up the tarp and wrote on it in marker: See you in December.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Do the thing. Play your cards. Do something. Look again. Stay weird. Make moments.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Do the thing you'd regret skipping. Play your cards. Do your something. Look again. Stay weird. Make moments.
Me, I'd sit on the couch. Someone has to guard the cocoa.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
